title: The stall watch never ends a quiet job whose process tree is alive, nor a lone sleep followed by a command; when it ends one, it kills the whole tree
why: hooks/stall_watch.py ends quiet-by-design background jobs and strands their processes: `merge --batch-build 104` ended twice with exit 3 while pid 27483 ran on under init; `sleep 420; gh api ...` ended before its read ran, though the waiter guard's own remedy allows one pause then a command; a piped `--batch-build` earlier (note no-pipe-long-merge).
source: batch runner 10, 10:13 CST Nov 12, via coordinator 10:13 CST; owner asked it be fixed
note: Debt, code. #2680 (step stall-watch-live-run) covers the live-CPU case only; this step holds the git-wait and lone-sleep cases and the whole-tree kill. Pairs with step kill-own-stranded-job. Ready, no lane. Narrowed to parts A and B (coordinator pick 11:05 CST Nov 12): git waiters and a lone sleep are not ended. The whole-tree kill is dropped: it would reverse decision stall-watch line 6 with nothing measured. PR 3558, the planned-wait fix (a leading sleep N before a command adds N seconds to the quiet time, so no STALL), merged 17:35 CST Nov 17 (REST read by triage 17:37 CST; merger unverified, merged_by is the shared login). No step names that PR. It matches this step's lone-sleep part by title only; triage read no diff, so pr stays 2862 and status stays doing.
